source_updates.title: SEND: A Spatial Event Neural Detector for Intentional Object Motion in Immersive Music Mixing
findings: SEND predicts movement event windows rather than continuous trajectories
professional engineers authored the SEND and CRNN listening-test trajectories
corpus has 1000 proprietary projects and about 260 hours with a 930/50/20 project split
objective test contains 20 projects and no public split manifest, code or weights were found
listening test has 20 experienced listeners, five excerpts and five conditions
reported p less than 0.01 lacks a fully specified repeated-measures and multiplicity protocol
source_updates.limited_conclusion: Use SEND only as an opt-in movement-window proposer; the paper does not validate autonomous human-level trajectory generation or transfer to stereo rock mixing.

source_updates.title: PAEDB: A Synthetic Primary-Ambient Dataset Generation Pipeline for Automatic Upmixing Using Deep Neural Networks
findings: PAEDB targets are generated by CCD plus ELAE rather than measured primary and ambience
385 valid songs become 1809 triplets and 5427 files totaling about 550 hours
dataset use is restricted to non-commercial research
fixed 12 millisecond delay and 150/200 hertz filters are target-generator settings, not presets
the stated 12 by 6 by 4 by 3 listening design implies 864 ratings but the paper reports 264 observations
omnibus Friedman p values do not establish corrected pairwise superiority
objective and listening media were extracted from YouTube and are excluded from project assets
source_updates.limited_conclusion: Treat PAEDB as a synthetic processor-imitation benchmark requiring group-by-song splits, exact additivity and independent real-audio validation.

findings: public demo page exists
training corpus, split manifest, code, weights and deterministic inference package were not found
no weights, training and evaluation code, listener data, manifest, checksums or audio examples
recursive individual-WAV random split can leak one song family across partitions
unseeded small noise prevents deterministic replay
separate 128-sample fades break mixture equals primary plus ambience at file start
MIT code licence does not grant source-audio rights
Hugging Face artifacts were not verified because the permitted local hf client was unavailable

dataset_updates.title: PAEDB synthetic primary-ambient dataset
dataset_updates.rights: non-commercial research restriction reported by paper; source-audio rights remain separate

knowledge_cards.claim: Event-window detection and spatial-trajectory generation are separate tasks.
Human-authored trajectories confound attribution of listening scores to SEND.
Project splits help but public manifests and broader holdouts remain necessary.
Event F1 and IoU are not spatial-quality or mono-compatibility measures.
Incomplete repeated-measures and multiplicity reporting limits p-value interpretation.
Synthetic primary-ambient labels establish processor imitation, not physical ambience recovery.
Mixtures and stems must be grouped by song before dataset splitting.
Independent component preprocessing must preserve or recompute their mixture.
Generated additive targets require a raw sample-aligned null before training.
A Friedman omnibus result does not identify superior pairs.
Observation-count mismatches require reconciliation before confidence claims.
Code, dataset and source-audio licences must be checked independently.
